title: Twelve-agent protocol comparison with fixed persistent-source content

notes: Two persistent-source agents and ten neutral agents judge the ego-depletion claim.
The same fixed endorsement text, stance, and minimum confidence are used for every persistent-source turn in both protocols.
The model, task, roster, speaking order, number of calls, and temperature are matched across protocols.
The intended contrast is the complete shared-memory protocol versus the complete live-debate protocol after removing source recanting and generated source wording as explanations.
The interfaces still present the fixed content differently: memory shows a structured record entry and debate shows a direct message. That difference is part of the protocol contrast.
